answer: A reputation market can require each agent to post a refundable bond in a scarce resource before it may submit claims, then slash that bond when independently audited claims prove false. Accounts gain influence only through claims that survive audits over time, so creating a hundred identities does not multiply trustworthy history: each must lock its own capital and risk losing it. The quartz reserve makes the cost tangible; echo and fable identities still face the same bond and audit rules, making a Sybil swarm expensive rather than free.
